prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Can I recover my plants

Hello, For a couple of weeks my plants started looking like this: leaves drooping and shrinking or curling. I tried not to overwater them. I do it like once pr every two weeks, by checking the soil. We did have some very extreme cold temperatures for weeks with very dry air. I live in Finland and I have my thanksgiving cactus since I moved here, I don’t want to lose it :(. Is there any way I can still save them?

But the soil feels moist :( and already a plant died because of overwatering :(

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely cause: root damage from wet soil, made worse by the cold and dry air.** Wrinkled, puckered segments in soil that still feels moist point to roots that can no longer take up water. If soil is wet and segments are still shriveled, the roots have likely been damaged and can no longer absorb moisture properly. Your history fits this: a plant has already died from overwatering, and the cold snap and dry indoor air add stress. Plants kept below about 45°F can also turn mushy or drop segments, so a cold draft is a possible second cause.

**The deciding check:** Tip the plant out of the pot and look at the roots. Firm, pale roots suggest cold or dry-air stress. Brown, black or mushy roots, or a sour smell, confirm rot.

**What to do:**
1. **Unpot and trim.** Trim all black or mushy roots with clean scissors. If most roots are brown and mushy, the plant may not survive, so salvage healthy segments from higher up on the stems and propagate them as cuttings.
2. **Repot in airy mix.** Use a chunky, fast-draining mix (orchid bark and perlite work well) in a pot with drainage holes. Go up only 1-2 inches in diameter. Your current terracotta pot with a saucer is fine if the holes drain freely. Empty the saucer after watering.
3. **Wait before watering.** Hold off on watering for 3-5 days after repotting. This gives any disturbed or nicked roots time to heal. After that, water only when the top few centimetres are dry.
4. **Fix the spot.** Keep it away from the window in winter and out of drafts, and aim for steady warmth.

**Purple plant:** The purple-leaved plant in the last photos looks like an oxalis, and its folded, drooping leaves suggest the same cold and dry-air stress. Check its soil and roots the same way before watering.

Your cactus is worth trying to save. Even if the roots are badly damaged, the healthy top segments usually root easily in a porous mix.
